text:
jonathan: Heads-up — customer on private VPC blocked egress to our eu-west model shard. Their control plane denies outbound to eu endpoints so runtime tried fallback and got a 403. App hit an unexpected hard error. Anyone seen this pattern?

tara: ugh. that's the onprem egress restriction case we talked about. did the runtime try a local quantized variant or just fall through to cloud?

jonathan: It attempted cloud fallback (model-neo-eu) first, 403 from their NAT. Then tried next variant but our router treats missing-region as non-compatible and returned error. No local-variant handshake.

lev: do we still have the "region-compat" preflight header idea? iirc it would let control plane indicate allowed egress before token-issuing.

maria: we prototyped a small control-plane handshake last quarter — returns allowed_regions + allow_fallback boolean. It lived in a branch. Example response we used in tests:
```
GET /v1/private/preflight?tenant=acme
Authorization: Bearer <kp>

200 OK
{
  "allowed_regions": ["us-west-2"],
  "allow_model_fallback": "local-first",
  "max_ttl": 300
}
```

sam: local-first meaning runtime should try on-prem quantized model first, then cloud variants if explicitly allowed?

maria: yes. and if allow_model_fallback == "none" we should never attempt cloud egress — return permission error on API call so caller can surface it.

lev: that solves policy, but UX in Console needs to show customers why requests failed and what fallback was attempted. otherwise support tickets blow up.

tara: agree. proposal: expose a compact rollout page per-tenant in Console > Private > Routing that shows: allowed regions, fallback policy, last 72h fallback attempts, and a one-click "generate local-variant" diagnostics bundle.

jonathan: also need to wire telemetry — sample token metadata with egress_decision and fallback_taken. Something like: `egress_decision=blocked` / `fallback=local` / `fallback_denied_by_policy`. Minimal PII.

ops-bot: new relic alert: tenant acme had 12 failed fallbacks in 10m.

sam: API-level change: runtime should call /v1/private/preflight (control plane) cached per-tenant for TTL. Then decision flow: if allowed_regions includes local_region -> route normally. else if allow_model_fallback == local-first -> attempt local variant. else return 403-like structured error with code `EGRESS_POLICY_BLOCK` and `meta.allowed_regions` in payload.

maria: question: what about multi-tenant hosts where onprem runtime can't access local quantized model? or customer didn't upload local model? need a clear error code for "no_local_variant_available" vs "egress_disallowed".

lev: yes split errors. Console should show recommended next steps: upload local model / change fallback policy / request exempted egress.

jonathan: security note — preflight mustn't leak region availability across tenants. Only return regions that are allowed for that tenant via their contract. Add scope check.

tara: rollout plan: feature-flag preflight handshake on control plane, enable runtime opt-in via config `private.preflight=true`, run canary with 10 tenants, monitor support volume and fallback telemetry for a week. deploy-bot will create canary wave.

deploy-bot: canary job queued: group=private-preflight-canary, wave=1, tenants=10.

sam: quick API sketch for error payload so SDKs can react:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "EGRESS_POLICY_BLOCK",
  "message": "Tenant egress policy prevents routing to eu-west-1",
  "meta": {"allowed_regions": ["us-west-2"], "recommended_action": "upload_local_variant_or_request_egress"}
}
```

maria: we also need to track policy changes in Audit logs for compliance. when an admin flips allow_model_fallback we should emit audit event.

lev: telemetry sampling: keep 1% of normal requests with full fallback trace, otherwise only counters per-tenant per-hour. prevents high-volume telemetry noise.

jonathan: action items: 1) maria & sam to revive preflight endpoint prototype and add scope checks (ETA 2d). 2) devex/console (tara) to mock the new UX card (ETA 4d). 3) lev to add SDK error handling for EGRESS_POLICY_BLOCK + tests (ETA 3d). 4) ops to schedule canary (deploy-bot already queued).

tara: thanks — i'll drop a short runbook snippet in #runbooks once UX mock exists.

jonathan: cool. if anyone has objections to the "local-first" default for private tenants speak now, otherwise we'll keep it.

maria: no objections from me. keeps customer apps resilient by default.

sam: +1

lev: +1

jonathan: ok closing thread, cc @support and @sales for visibility.
